chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom. When I fulfilled my rituals for the Umrah, I went to my wife and I had not shortened (my hair/nails).' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon you is a camel.' I said: 'When I intended that from her, and she had not shortened, she prevented me. But when I overcame her, she cut some of her hair with her teeth.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'May Allah have mercy on her. She is more understanding than you. Upon you is a camel, and there is nothing upon her.'
ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a man who has intercourse with his wife before shortening his hair after Umrah?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the expiation (Damm) for a Muhrim who engages in marital relations before performing Qasr, ruling that the husband bears the penalty while the wife is exempt due to her ignorance of the ruling. The Imam’s praise of his wife as 'more learned' (afqaha) highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the wife’s independent religious status and how her lack of knowledge serves as a valid excuse (‘udhr) distinct from the husband’s obligation. This ruling underscores the principle that the primary penalty for breaking the state of Ihram through intercourse falls on the male performer, while the female partner is not penalized if she acted in good faith.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! When I fulfilled my rituals for the Umra, I went over to my wife and I had not shortened (hair, nails etc.)’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Upon you is a camel’. I said, ‘When I intended that from her, and she herself had not shortened, so she prevented me. But when I overcame her, she cut some of her hair with her teeth’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> have Mercy on her. She is of more understanding than you are. Upon you is a camel, and there is nothing upon her’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, I completed the acts of my al-‘Umrah and went to my wife before Taqsir (cutting some hair or finger nails and so on). He (the Imam) said, ‘You owe a badanah.’ I then said, ’When I wanted it she had not done Taqsir (cutting some hair or finger nails and so on) yet, she refused but I over- powered her. She cut something from her hairs with her teeth. He (the Imam) said, ‘Allah has blessed her; she was more knowledgeable in Shari‘ah than you. You owe one badanah but she is not obligated for anything in this matter.”’
